slot.brief: Show a velocity–time graph (multi-segment, including a negative-velocity portion) of a particle; ask for the displacement or distance travelled in the full time interval, or average speed, requiring careful signed areas.

stem: For the velocity–time graph shown, find the particle's displacement and distance travelled, respectively, during the interval shown.

verdicts.working: Signed area: 6 + 18 + 4 − 4 − 1 = 23 m. Total absolute area: 6 + 18 + 4.5 + 0.5 + 4 + 1 = 34 m.

solution:
Displacement is the signed area under the velocity–time graph; distance is the sum of the absolute areas. Thus,
$$\Delta x=28.5-5.5=23\ \text{m},\qquad s=28.5+5.5=34\ \text{m}$$

draft.stem: For the velocity–time graph shown, find the particle's displacement and distance travelled, respectively, during the interval shown.

figure.description: Draw perpendicular axes with horizontal axis labeled $t$ (s) and vertical axis labeled $v$ (m s$^{-1}$); mark $v=0$ as the horizontal axis. Mark time ticks at $0,2,5,7,9,10$ and velocity ticks at $-2,0,6$. Join these points in order by straight segments: $(0,0)$, $(2,6)$, $(5,6)$, $(7,-2)$, $(9,-2)$, $(10,0)$. Label each vertex with its coordinate $(t,v)$.

draft.distractor_notes: A: uses signed area for distance as well as displacement. B: ignores the below-axis area when calculating displacement. D: adds unsigned areas to obtain displacement.
